games.name: CONTROL PANEL
games.character_role: A circular emotion portrait sits on a dark rounded-square plate above the options, and the current word chunk is printed across its face. The angry red 'my boss' (phone start) becomes an orange 'yelled at' (phone mid), then a purple swirl 'panic' (phone finish). It swaps per chunk only. It does not react to ACT NOW, PLAN IT and the other choices, and it ends on panic rather than calm. On desktop it is a 40 px decal.
games.finale: The phone finish tile is identical to the mid tile ('SELECTED: ACT NOW', with a dark toast pill over the ACT NOW card), so nothing marks finishing. Phone reveal: the shared reveal card ('RELEASE COMPLETE +N STILL / <NAME> / STEADIER + a stock line / FEEL A SHIFT? YES / NOT YET / AGAIN' with PREVIOUS/NEXT pills) on the empty nebula, the same layout in every game in this batch ('STEADIER, THE MESS GOT SIMPLER'). The desktop reveal tile renders only the PREVIOUS/NEXT pills with no card at all. It is not unique.
games.score_rationale: A4: the option cards are glossy cyan-magenta gradient slabs with an orb highlight (phone start). They are clean, but they read as default UI, with no console materials or light. B3: a button grid on the shared nebula, with no switchboard, dials or levers. C2: plain taps, and the chosen card is replaced by a dark toast pill whose headline ('YESSS', 'NICE ONE') is about 5 px (phone mid/finish). There is no switch throw or anticipation. D3: a per-chunk portrait decal (see character_role). E2: the finish tile is unchanged from mid, and the reveal card is shared or missing on desktop. F4: the instruction is readable and the labels are large on phone. However, the 5th option RELEASE IT is hidden behind the Live Guide panel (phone start, a sliver at y~585), 'SELECTED: ACT NOW' never changes across 6 rounds, and the desktop labels are about 6-7 px. G3: the hidden 5th option, the clipped header, and toasts covering ACT NOW (phone mid/finish). H4: turning a worry into a next action fits anxiety, but ASK HELP and PLAN IT lead nowhere, so the choice has no follow-through.

games.strengths: A clear, therapeutically useful question ('what do you want to do with this thought?'). The phone option cards are big thumb targets with two-line labels. The game finishes on both sizes with no errors.
games.problems: Phone start tile: the RELEASE IT option is cut off behind the Live Guide panel, so only 4 of 5 controls are visible. All phone tiles: the user word sits on the portrait's face, which breaks the bubble rule, and the portrait sits on a dark square plate. Phone mid/finish tiles: the chosen card turns into a dark pill with unreadable micro text, and 'DO IT TODAY' ghosts through underneath. The Live Guide 'How to play' row is blank in the mid tile. phone header title is clipped ('MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO') and the LVL chip overlaps 'by THINKSTILL' (all phone tiles). Desktop tiles: a small centred panel with about 6 px labels, and an empty reveal (85_1280_reveal shows only PREVIOUS/NEXT).
improvements: Rebuild it as a physical control console: five chunky toggle levers or big illuminated switches on a brushed-metal desk with warm under-glow. Each throw needs anticipation (the lever resists, then snaps with squash) plus a click sound and a bulb lighting up.

Give each choice a visible consequence. ACT NOW drops a glowing task card into an 'outbox'. PLAN IT pins the card to a calendar strip. PARK IT slides it into a labelled drawer. ASK HELP sends a paper plane to a helper character. RELEASE IT vents it as steam through a chimney.

Make the emotion character the console operator. It sits at the desk, flinches at the incoming worry and leans over to watch each lever. It visibly loosens from red and clenched to warm and smiling as the outbox fills.
Finale: the console wires light up board-wide, the outbox prints a tidy 'my next moves' ticket, and the operator spins in the chair and gives a thumbs-up. The shared card follows after it.
Fix the layout: fit all 5 options above the Live Guide at 390 px (a 3+2 grid or a horizontal lever rail). Move the user word onto a caption strip below the portrait, and drop the dark square plate.
Keep the toast pills off the controls (anchor them in the top band) and make their headline at least 15 px. Fix the desktop reveal so the card actually renders.
games.looks_like: Same portrait-above-option-grid layout as 86 and 88. Its choice mechanic is in the catalog look-alike cluster with 32, 83 and 73.

games.strengths: A good therapeutic concept, with the strongest portrait rendering in the batch (phone start). Three large touch targets, and progress (42% to 100%) and the 1/6 to 6/6 round count advance correctly.
games.problems: Phone start/mid/finish tiles: the stamp buttons have no text labels at all, only a handle-and-pad icon. All phone tiles: the chunk word is printed over the character's face, which breaks the bubble rule. Phone mid tile: the 'YESSS + STILL HIT · CHAIN x3' toast sits on the FACT stamp. improvements: Label every stamp with a large word (FACT / STORY / UNSURE at 16 px or more), give each a distinct ink colour, and put a ghost stamp mark on the paper as a preview.
Feed whole claims, not single words: split the input into 2-4 short statements such as 'my boss yelled at me' and 'I will be fired', each on a paper slip sliding onto a desk.

Build a warm-lit wooden desk under a lamp. The press needs anticipation (the stamp lifts), a heavy squash on impact, an ink splat with a paper bounce, and a thump sound. STORY slips curl and float off as paper birds; FACT slips stack neatly.
Make the character a clerk at the desk. It squints at each slip, nods at FACT, and laughs and relaxes when a STORY slip flies away. Its face should move from tense to amused across the round.
